title: kbgit.py publish fast-forwards the public home
goal: kbgit.py publish keeps its projection and fast-forward rules and also refuses (exit 1, naming the cause, nothing pushed) when the integration CI verdict of the source commit is not ok (ql_deliver.ci_pipeline: red, pending, none, or skip when glab or gh cannot read it), when the projection's tree holds a root whose _root.md says visibility: internal or any path under a _private or _cache directory, or when a file the projection changes against the public tip has a leak-scan hit (kbcommon.leak_hits with _tools/tests_allowlist.txt); kbgit.py publish --hook, run by an async SessionStart hook beside red-pipeline, publishes silently in a clone with a publish remote, prints only a refusal, and does nothing without one; tests.py -k TestPublishSafety plants each refusal and -k TestPublishHook the hook

gates.question: May kbgit.py publish push main to the publish remote (the public home)?
options: yes, fast-forward only, after a green integration main
yes, but only by a person running the command
no: the public home is updated by hand
gates.recommendation: yes, fast-forward only, after a green integration main
gates.answer: yes, fast-forward only, after a green integration main

gates.question: When does publish run? This replaces the sprints' github gate answer (at sprint close only).
options: at sprint close by the orchestrator, and by a person any time
gates.recommendation: at sprint close by the orchestrator, and by a person any time

gates.question: Which content may reach the public home?
options: public roots and the code; never an internal root, _private/, _cache/ or a leak-scan hit (refused, not filtered)
the same, but internal roots are stripped from a published branch instead of refused
gates.recommendation: public roots and the code; never an internal root, _private/, _cache/ or a leak-scan hit (refused, not filtered)
gates.answer: public roots and the code; never an internal root, _private/, _cache/ or a leak-scan hit (refused, not filtered)

gates.question: What runs publish after every green integration main?
options: the async SessionStart hook in each maintainer clone, beside red-pipeline: no credential in CI, publishes at the next session after main turns green
a CI job on the integration main with a deploy key for the public home: publishes within the pipeline, the key is a CI secret
a push mirror set on the integration host: no tool code, but it mirrors without the green or public-content checks
gates.recommendation: the async SessionStart hook in each maintainer clone, beside red-pipeline: no credential in CI, publishes at the next session after main turns green
gates.answer: the async SessionStart hook in each maintainer clone, beside red-pipeline: no credential in CI, publishes at the next session after main turns green

notes: kbgit.py publish exists (kbpublic.py; git.md, Public home): it pushes the projection of the integration main without kb/_querylog as a fast-forward, refuses a public tip that is not an ancestor unless --rewrite, and prints a note without a publish remote; TestPublish covers that, so the checks name new classes. The projection keeps filtering the query-log store; the public-content answer (refused, not filtered) covers internal roots, _private/, _cache/ and leak-scan hits. 'Green' is ql_deliver.pipeline_verdict's ok: optional manual jobs never make a pipeline failed (automated-merge-requests.md:34, :66), so while the GitLab jobs are manual a green main says only that nothing failed (every job is manual, so nothing runs on its own). A push mirror cannot stand in for publish: it has no path filter (repository-mirroring.md:38). On GitHub, restrict updates with a bypass for the publisher can make publish the only writer of the public main (github-branch-rules-and-auto-merge.md:39): optional host setup for git.md, no tool change. Each publish is a pure function of the source history, so sessions that publish the same main at once agree.
